events_in_time_windows.name: events_in_time_windows
events_in_time_windows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required output columns for the view
  e.user_pseudo_id AS pseudo_user_id,
  e.event_timestamp,
  -- engagement_time: lift specific metric literal OUT of view; here we select the common GA4 engagement metric if present in event_params.
  -- We extract parameter named "engagement_time_msec" (typical GA4 name) as raw integer milliseconds; null if absent.
  (
    SELECT
      SAFE_CAST(ep.value.int_value AS INT64)
    FROM UNNEST(e.event_params) AS ep
    WHERE ep.key = 'engagement_time_msec'
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS engagement_time
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ga4_obfuscated_sample_ecommerce.events_*` AS e
WHERE
  -- Keep only events that fall within either:
  --  (1) the 7-day window ending at the target timestamp (placeholder: @target_ts_millis, lift out of view)
  --  OR
  --  (2) the 2-day window ending at the target timestamp
  --
  -- The view expects the caller to provide:
  --   @target_ts_millis INT64  -- target timestamp in milliseconds since epoch
  --   @two_day_millis INT64    -- duration of 2 days in milliseconds (e.g. 2*24*3600*1000)
  --   @seven_day_millis INT64  -- duration of 7 days in milliseconds (e.g. 7*24*3600*1000)
  --
  -- Timestamp comparison uses event_timestamp (stored in milliseconds).
  (
    e.event_timestamp BETWEEN (@target_ts_millis - @seven_day_millis) AND @target_ts_millis
    OR
    e.event_timestamp BETWEEN (@target_ts_millis - @two_day_millis) AND @target_ts_millis
  )
  -- Restrict wildcard shards by table suffix range as documented (lifted out of view):
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20201101' AND '20210131'
events_in_time_windows.description: Select all event rows that fall within either the 7-day window or the 2-day window ending at the target timestamp. Keep the event timestamp, pseudo user id, and engagement time metric (raw).

visitors_who_bought_target.name: visitors_who_bought_target
visitors_who_bought_target.body_sql:
SELECT
  DISTINCT CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit,
  UNNEST(hit.product) AS prod
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170701' AND '20170731'
  AND prod.v2ProductName = 'Youtube Men’s Vintage Henley'
  AND SAFE_CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) IS NOT NULL
visitors_who_bought_target.description: Identify distinct visitors who purchased at least one product whose name equals the target product ('Youtube Men’s Vintage Henley') within July 2017. One row per visitor who meets that condition.

sessions_2017.name: sessions_2017
sessions_2017.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", COALESCE(fullVisitorId, CAST(visitorId AS STRING))) AS STRING) AS session_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  STRUCT(
    trafficSource.source AS source,
    trafficSource.medium AS medium,
    trafficSource.campaign AS campaign,
    trafficSource.referralPath AS referralPath
  ) AS traffic_source,
  COALESCE(totals.transactionRevenue, 0) / 1e6 AS transaction_revenue
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20171231'
  AND date BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20171231'
sessions_2017.description: Select session-level rows limited to calendar year 2017, preserving session date, traffic source field, and transaction revenue for each session.

visitor_first_visit_in_feb.name: visitor_first_visit_in_feb
visitor_first_visit_in_feb.body_sql:
SELECT
  fullVisitorId,
  MIN(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date)) AS first_visit_date_in_feb_2017
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170201' AND '20170228'
GROUP BY
  fullVisitorId
visitor_first_visit_in_feb.description: For each visitor (fullVisitorId), compute the earliest session_date in February 2017 (their first visit date in Feb). One row per visitor.

sessions_hits_products_sel.name: sessions_hits_products_sel
sessions_hits_products_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "_", CAST(visitNumber AS STRING)) AS session_id,
  date AS date,
  COALESCE(trafficSource.source, '') AS source,
  COALESCE(trafficSource.medium, '') AS source_medium,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS hit_date,
  COALESCE(prod.productSKU, '') AS product_id,
  COALESCE(prod.productRevenue, 0) AS product_revenue
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h,
  UNNEST(h.product) AS prod
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170630'
sessions_hits_products_sel.description: Select sessions restricted to the date range (2017-01-01 through 2017-06-30) and unnest/emit hits-level product rows so each row represents a single product occurrence on a single hit within a session. Include session identifiers, date, source/source_medium, hit timestamp or hit date, productRevenue (as recorded on the hit-level product), and any fields needed for day/week/month bucketing. Treat missing productRevenue as zero where appropriate (do not aggregate yet).

sessions_filtered_by_date.name: sessions_filtered_by_date
sessions_filtered_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  date AS session_date,
  COALESCE(totals.transactions, 0) AS transactions,
  COALESCE(
    -- sum product revenue from hits.product.productRevenue where present; fall back to totals.transactionRevenue
    (SELECT SUM(IFNULL(p.productRevenue, 0)) FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h, UNNEST(h.product) AS p),
    IFNULL(totals.transactionRevenue, 0)
  ) AS productRevenue,
  COALESCE(totals.pageviews, 0) AS pageviews,
  CAST(visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
sessions_filtered_by_date.description: Select sessions that fall within the target date range (no classification yet). Keep raw session fields needed later such as session date, transactions, productRevenue, pageviews, and visitor identifier.

jan2017_session_hits_filtered.name: jan2017_session_hits_filtered
jan2017_session_hits_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session_id: use visitId to represent session_id, carry through
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "_", _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS STRING) AS session_id,
  -- visitor_id: fullVisitorId
  fullVisitorId AS visitor_id,
  -- session_date: date field from table (YYYYMMDD)
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS session_date,
  -- hit_id: unique per hit: combine visitId and hitNumber and table suffix
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(visitId AS STRING), "-", CAST(h.hitNumber AS STRING), "_", _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS STRING) AS hit_id,
  -- hit_timestamp: compute seconds since epoch from visitStartTime + hit.time (both in seconds)
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime + h.time) AS hit_timestamp,
  -- page_path: page.pagePath if present, else NULL
  h.page.pagePath AS page_path,
  -- campaign: trafficSource.campaign
  trafficSource.campaign AS campaign
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*` ,
  UNNEST(hits) AS h
WHERE
  -- restrict to January 2017 shards
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170101' AND '20170131'
  -- only visitors whose campaign contains 'Data Share' (case-sensitive per requirement; use SAFE accordingly)
  AND trafficSource.campaign LIKE '%Data Share%'
  -- keep all hits for those sessions; but ensure we output hit rows (no extra filter on page_path)
  -- however we include only hits that have a page path or any hit (we keep all to find the next hit)
  -- include only rows where hit has a page struct or other hit types: allow NULL pagePath

semantic_filters.pagepath_scope: include hits for sessions that have any hit, but page_path values are kept as-is; downstream steps will select hits where page_path starts with '/home' when determining transitions

jan2017_session_hits_filtered.description: Filter raw hit-level events to sessions in Jan 2017, only hits from visitors whose campaign name contains the substring 'Data Share', and only include hits whose page path starts with '/home' or any other page path (we keep all hits for those sessions so we can find the next hit). This is the session-level hit cohort to consider.

sessions_filtered.name: sessions_filtered
sessions_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(visitId AS STRING) AS session_id,
  CAST(visitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', date) AS session_date,
  COALESCE(totals.pageviews, 0) AS pageviews,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS(
    SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(hits) AS h WHERE h.transaction.transactionId IS NOT NULL
  ) OR totals.transactions IS NOT NULL AND totals.transactions > 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_transaction_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20170601' AND '20170731'
  AND totals.pageviews IS NOT NULL
sessions_filtered.description: Filter sessions to the date range 2017-06-01..2017-07-31 inclusive and exclude sessions with NULL pageviews. Keep fields required to classify and attribute pageviews (session id, visitor id, session_date, pageviews, transaction indicator).

user_first_visit_events.name: user_first_visit_events
user_first_visit_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS user_id,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime) AS first_visit_datetime
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
QUALIFY
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY fullVisitorId ORDER BY visitStartTime ASC) = 1
user_first_visit_events.description: For each user, find their earliest visit event datetime (the first visit) and retain any device/type info from that event if needed.

visits_sel.name: visits_sel
visits_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING) AS visitor_id,
  TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(visitStartTime) AS visit_timestamp,
  date AS visit_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample.ga_sessions_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20160801' AND '20170801'
visits_sel.description: Select raw visit events/records needed to determine each user's first visit date. This isolates visitor identifier and visit timestamp/date (and any fields needed for canonicalization).

inpatient_2014_rows.name: inpatient_2014_rows
inpatient_2014_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  provider_city AS city,
  total_discharges,
  average_total_payments AS total_payments
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
inpatient_2014_rows.description: Filter the CMS Medicare inpatient charges data to only rows from year 2014. Keep all columns needed for DRG definition, city, total discharges, and total payments.

drg_total_discharges.name: drg_total_discharges
drg_total_discharges.body_sql:
SELECT
  drg_definition,
  SUM(total_discharges) AS sum_discharges_drg
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
GROUP BY
  drg_definition
drg_total_discharges.description: Compute total discharges per DRG definition across all cities (sum of per-row discharges in 2014) to identify which DRG has the largest overall discharges.

prescriptions_2014.name: prescriptions_2014
prescriptions_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  total_claim_count AS prescription_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE("2014-01-01")) = 2014  -- year literal lifted out; ensures view conceptually for 2014
  AND nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
prescriptions_2014.description: Restrict raw prescription records to rows for the year 2014 and to rows that have a non-null US state identifier; keep medication identifier/name and the prescription quantity/count value for each record.

medication_counts_by_state.name: medication_counts_by_state
medication_counts_by_state.body_sql:
SELECT
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  drug_name AS medication,
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(total_claim_count) AS INT64) AS total_prescription_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  nppes_provider_state,
  drug_name
medication_counts_by_state.description: Aggregate the 2014 prescription records to compute the total prescription count per medication within each state.

provider_cost_records_2014.name: provider_cost_records_2014
provider_cost_records_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  'inpatient' AS cost_type,
  average_medicare_payments AS avg_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
UNION ALL
SELECT
  provider_id,
  provider_name,
  'outpatient' AS cost_type,
  average_total_payments AS avg_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2014'
provider_cost_records_2014.description: Select all cost records for the year 2014 restricted to records that represent outpatient or inpatient average costs. Keep provider identifier, provider name, cost type (outpatient vs inpatient), and the average cost value for that record.

provider_combined_average.name: provider_combined_average
provider_combined_average.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(o.provider_id, i.provider_id) AS provider_id,
  COALESCE(o.provider_name, i.provider_name) AS provider_name,
  -- outpatient average cost comes from outpatient_charges_* average_estimated_submitted_charges
  o.outpatient_avg_cost,
  -- inpatient average cost comes from inpatient_charges_* average_medicare_payments
  i.inpatient_avg_cost,
  -- combined is sum of the two averages; lift any literal (none) out of view
  SAFE_ADD(o.outpatient_avg_cost, i.inpatient_avg_cost) AS combined_average
FROM
  (
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      ANY_VALUE(provider_name) AS provider_name,
      AVG(average_estimated_submitted_charges) AS outpatient_avg_cost
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.outpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
    GROUP BY provider_id
  ) o
FULL JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      provider_id,
      ANY_VALUE(provider_name) AS provider_name,
      AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS inpatient_avg_cost
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
    GROUP BY provider_id
  ) i
USING (provider_id)
provider_combined_average.description: Compute the combined average cost per provider by summing the outpatient and inpatient average cost columns; produce one row per provider with both averages and the combined_average value.

drug_claims_2014_by_record.name: drug_claims_2014_by_record
drug_claims_2014_by_record.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- drug identifier: prefer generic_name if present, else drug_name
  COALESCE(generic_name, drug_name) AS drug_id,
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  total_claim_count AS claim_count,
  total_drug_cost AS drug_cost,
  -- carry-through key to keep row-level joinable (claim_record_id = concatenation of npi + drug + row identifier)
  CONCAT(npi, '|', drug_name, '|', CAST(total_claim_count AS STRING), '|2014') AS claim_record_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
drug_claims_2014_by_record.description: Select all prescription claim records for the year 2014 with relevant fields (drug identifier, state, claim count for that record, drug cost for that record). This is a row-level cohort of claims in 2014.

ny_drug_prescriptions_2014.name: ny_drug_prescriptions_2014
ny_drug_prescriptions_2014.body_sql:
SELECT
  SAFE_CAST(generic_name AS STRING) AS drug_id,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS ny_total_claims
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
GROUP BY
  drug_id
ny_drug_prescriptions_2014.description: Aggregate 2014 claim records restricted to New York State to compute total prescriptions (total claim counts) per drug in NY during 2014.

top_ny_drug_state_ranking.name: top_ny_drug_state_ranking
top_ny_drug_state_ranking.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry drug identifier and name so view is joinable; drug_name from table is treated as drug_id
  drug_name AS drug_id,
  nppes_provider_state AS state,
  SUM(total_claim_count) AS state_total_claims,
  SUM(total_drug_cost) AS state_total_drug_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
WHERE
  nppes_provider_state = 'NY' -- liftable literal: identify drug(s) with max total prescriptions in NY first
GROUP BY
  drug_name,
  nppes_provider_state
HAVING
  -- keep only the drug(s) whose NY total_claim_count equals the maximum across drugs in NY
  SUM(total_claim_count) = (
    SELECT
      MAX(drug_claims) FROM (
        SELECT
          SUM(total_claim_count) AS drug_claims
        FROM
          `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.part_d_prescriber_2014`
        WHERE
          nppes_provider_state = 'NY'
        GROUP BY
          drug_name
      )
  )
top_ny_drug_state_ranking.description: Identify the single drug(s) with the maximum total prescriptions in NY (from ny_drug_prescriptions_2014), join that drug to the per-state aggregates, and produce per-state rows for that drug. (Final filtering, ordering by state_total_claims DESC and limiting to top 5 is applied at query time.)

provider_year_averages.name: provider_year_averages
provider_year_averages.body_sql:
SELECT
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS yearly_avg_inpatient_cost,
  AVG(average_total_payments) AS yearly_avg_outpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  year
UNION ALL
SELECT
  provider_id,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  AVG(average_medicare_payments) AS yearly_avg_inpatient_cost,
  NULL AS yearly_avg_outpatient_cost
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_medicare.inpatient_charges_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2015'
GROUP BY
  provider_id,
  year
provider_year_averages.description: For each provider and year, compute the yearly averages: average of record inpatient_cost and average of record outpatient_cost (using only that provider's records in that year).
counter_examples: For the provider whose total inpatient Medicare cost from 2011 through 2015 is the highest (computed as the sum of average_medicare_payments multiplied by total_discharges), please list that provider’s yearly average inpatient cost and yearly average outpatient cost for each calendar year in this period, where the inpatient cost is calculated as the average of (average_medicare_payments × total_discharges) and the outpatient cost is calculated as the average of (average_total_payments × outpatient_services).

participants_cohort.name: participants_cohort
participants_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT CAST(person_id AS INT64) AS person_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`
participants_cohort.description: All distinct participants in the dataset; one row per participant to define the denominator.

icd10cm_standard_concepts.name: icd10cm_standard_concepts
icd10cm_standard_concepts.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical numeric id derived from the ICD-10-CM code string (keep as string here to preserve joinability)
  cm_code AS condition_standard_concept_id,
  short_description AS condition_standard_concept_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_codes.icd10_diagnoses_2019`
WHERE
  -- lift the target codes out as literals; this view returns only the standard concepts for these codes
  cm_code IN ('L70', 'L20', 'L40', 'L80')
icd10cm_standard_concepts.description: The set of standard ICD-10-CM concept records for the target codes (L70, L20, L40, L80). One row per standard concept; used as the seeds for descendant mapping and to carry canonical id and label.

concept_descendants.name: concept_descendants
concept_descendants.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- seed standard ICD-10-CM concept id (the "condition_standard_concept_id")
  seed.concept_id AS condition_standard_concept_id,
  -- descendant concept id reachable via descendant/child relationships (including the seed itself)
  descendant.concept_id AS descendant_concept_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS seed
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_relationship` AS rel
  ON rel.concept_id_1 = seed.concept_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept` AS descendant
  ON descendant.concept_id = rel.concept_id_2
WHERE
  -- only consider seed concepts that are standard and from ICD-10-CM vocabulary
  seed.standard_concept = 'S'
  AND seed.vocabulary_id = 'ICD10CM'
  -- relationship types that represent descendant/child links:
  -- include common descendant relationship ids; lift literals out of callers if they need different set
  AND rel.relationship_id IN ('Is a', 'Subsumes', 'Has descendant', 'Maps to')
concept_descendants.description: All descendant concepts (including the seed standard concept itself) reachable from each seed standard ICD-10-CM concept via concept_relationships that define descendant/child links. One row per (seed_standard_concept, descendant_concept) mapping to allow mapping clinical records to the seed standard concept.

participant_condition_counts.name: participant_condition_counts
participant_condition_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  ca.ancestor_concept_id AS condition_standard_concept_id,
  co.person_id AS person_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` AS ca
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.condition_occurrence` AS co
ON
  ca.descendant_concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
GROUP BY
  ca.ancestor_concept_id,
  co.person_id
participant_condition_counts.description: For each seed standard concept and participant, indicate whether the participant has at least one record mapped to the seed or any of its descendants. One row per (condition_standard_concept_id, person_id) after de-duplication; used to count distinct participants per condition.

all_participants.name: all_participants
all_participants.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(person_id AS STRING) AS participant_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.person`
all_participants.description: All participants in the dataset to be considered as the denominator (one row per participant). This relation selects the canonical participant identifier for every person in scope, applying no additional demographic/time filters.

medication_records.name: medication_records
medication_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- participant identifier from drug_exposure.person_id
  CAST(de.drug_exposure_id AS STRING) AS participant_id,  -- kept as string to carry joinable id; will be remapped outside view
  de.drug_exposure_id AS medication_record_id,
  -- Map medication record to an RxCUI-like identifier: use drug_concept_id as med_rxcui
  de.drug_concept_id AS med_rxcui,
  -- related_medication_flag: TRUE if there exists a matching drug_strength record
  -- (indicates a related medication strength/ingredient record exists)
  IF(ds.drug_concept_id IS NOT NULL OR ds.ingredient_concept_id IS NOT NULL, TRUE, FALSE) AS related_medication_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_strength` ds
ON
  de.drug_concept_id = ds.drug_concept_id
medication_records.description: All medication exposure records (prescriptions, dispenses, medication orders, or mapped medication concepts) for participants. Include fields that link a medication record to a participant and to an RxCUI or related medication identifier; do not collapse multiple records yet.

participant_quinapril_usage.name: participant_quinapril_usage
participant_quinapril_usage.body_sql:
SELECT
  de.person_id AS participant_id,
  EXISTS(
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure` de2
    WHERE de2.person_id = de.person_id
      AND (
        -- direct quinapril RxCUI equivalence: drug_concept_id = 35208
        de2.drug_concept_id = 35208
        -- OR drug mapped via ingredient/related concept: join through drug_strength ingredient_concept_id
        OR EXISTS(
          SELECT 1
          FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_strength` ds
          WHERE ds.drug_concept_id = de2.drug_concept_id
            AND ds.ingredient_concept_id = 35208
        )
        -- OR drug is a descendant of quinapril in the concept_ancestor table
        OR EXISTS(
          SELECT 1
          FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.concept_ancestor` ca
          WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 35208
            AND ca.descendant_concept_id = de2.drug_concept_id
        )
      )
  ) AS uses_quinapril_or_related
FROM (
  -- base set of participants who have any drug_exposure record
  SELECT DISTINCT person_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cms_synthetic_patient_data_omop.drug_exposure`
) de
participant_quinapril_usage.description: Determine, for each participant, whether they have any medication record that is quinapril or a related medication (RxCUI = 35208 or flagged as related). One row per participant with a boolean/flag indicating 'uses_quinapril_or_related'.

tracks_points_sel.name: tracks_points_sel
tracks_points_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid AS storm_id,

  latitude,

  CAST(SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(season, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS INT64) AS year,
  usa_status AS status
FROM

WHERE
  iso_time IS NOT NULL
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
tracks_points_sel.description: Select raw track points for storms, restricted to observations that have timestamped coordinates; each row is one recorded track point (latitude, longitude, timestamp) for a storm lifecycle entry.
validated_on: Can you provide the latitude of the final coordinates for the hurricane that traveled the second longest distance in the North Atlantic during 2020?

storm_tracks_raw.name: storm_tracks_raw
storm_tracks_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid AS storm_id,

  iso_time AS observation_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  usa_wind AS max_sustained_wind,
  basin,

storm_tracks_raw.description: Select all tracking-point records for storms in the North Atlantic basin during the 2020 season, excluding records with NULL coordinates or NULL observation time. Keep storm identifiers, observation time, latitude, longitude, and max sustained wind at that observation.

daily_valid_temp_flags_2019.name: daily_valid_temp_flags_2019
daily_valid_temp_flags_2019.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, "-", wban) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  -- temp field: missing value encoded as 9999.9 per DDL
  CASE WHEN temp IS NOT NULL AND temp != 9999.9 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS temp_present,
  -- max and min fields: missing encoded as 9999.9 per DDL
  CASE WHEN max IS NOT NULL AND max != 9999.9 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS tmax_present,
  CASE WHEN min IS NOT NULL AND min != 9999.9 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS tmin_present,
  -- valid day if all three present
  CASE
    WHEN (temp IS NOT NULL AND temp != 9999.9)
     AND (max IS NOT NULL AND max != 9999.9)
     AND (min IS NOT NULL AND min != 9999.9)
    THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE
  END AS valid_temp_day_2019
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2019'
daily_valid_temp_flags_2019.description: All daily station observations in calendar year 2019 with flags indicating whether temp, tmax, and tmin are non-missing and a combined flag for a valid temperature-record day (temp AND tmax AND tmin all present).

june12_observations_by_year.name: june12_observations_by_year
june12_observations_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS station_id,        -- keep key/id for joinability
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  -- temperatures in gsod are in Fahrenheit; missing indicated by 9999.9 -> null
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temperature,
  -- wind speed stored in wdsp (string in some years) and/or wdsp numeric; coerce to float and treat 999.9 as missing
  NULLIF(CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64), 999.9) AS wind_speed,
  -- precipitation prcp missing = 99.99
  NULLIF(prcp, 99.99) AS precipitation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
  AND CAST(year AS INT64) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
  -- restrict to June 12 of each year
  AND CAST(mo AS INT64) = 6
  AND CAST(da AS INT64) = 12
  -- filter to a single target station: lift literal OUT of the view per instructions.
  -- Users should add a WHERE clause on station_id when querying the view, e.g. WHERE CONCAT(stn,'-',wban) = 'XXXX-YYYY'
june12_observations_by_year.description: Restrict normalized observations to the target station and to the specific years of interest (2011 through 2020) and ensure the date corresponds to June 12 of the extracted year.

date_filtered_records.name: date_filtered_records
date_filtered_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  latitude AS latitude,
  longitude AS longitude,
  DATE(timestamp) AS date,
  AVG(CAST(speed AS FLOAT64)) OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(timestamp), _TABLE_SUFFIX) AS daily_average_wind_speed,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS source_table_name,
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, ":", CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY timestamp, latitude, longitude) AS STRING)) AS row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.wind_reports*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @start_table_suffix AND @end_table_suffix
  AND timestamp BETWEEN @start_timestamp AND @end_timestamp
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND speed IS NOT NULL
date_filtered_records.description: Filter the normalized rows to the requested date range (inclusive). This produces the cohort within the period of interest but still does not apply final ordering/limit.

gsod_2022_records.name: gsod_2022_records
gsod_2022_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS usaf,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9), CAST(9999.9 AS FLOAT64)) AS temp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(max, 9999.9), CAST(9999.9 AS FLOAT64)) AS max_temp,
  NULLIF(NULLIF(min, 9999.9), CAST(9999.9 AS FLOAT64)) AS min_temp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2022'
  AND stn <> '999999'
gsod_2022_records.description: Select all GSOD observations dated in 2022, excluding records whose station identifier (USAF) equals the literal '999999'. Do not aggregate — keep one row per original observation/record.

station_daily_valid_counts.name: station_daily_valid_counts
station_daily_valid_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf,
  COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(records.date)) AS valid_days_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS s
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` AS records
  ON records.stn = s.usaf
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATE(records.date)) = 2022
  -- normalized missing sentinel for temp is 9999.9 per schema; treat anything other than 9999.9 as valid
  AND records.temp IS NOT NULL
  AND records.temp != 9999.9
GROUP BY
  s.usaf
station_daily_valid_counts.description: Aggregate the normalized daily-valid flags to one row per station and calendar day to determine whether the station has at least one valid temperature observation for that day; then count the number of distinct calendar days in 2022 with at least one valid temperature record for each station.

stations_validity_status.name: stations_validity_status
stations_validity_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.usaf AS usaf,
  COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(CONCAT(g.year,'-',LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'),'-',LPAD(g.da,2,'0')))) AS valid_days_total,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(CONCAT(g.year,'-',LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'),'-',LPAD(g.da,2,'0')))), 365) AS valid_fraction_of_365,
  IF(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(CONCAT(g.year,'-',LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'),'-',LPAD(g.da,2,'0')))), 365) >= 0.90, TRUE, FALSE) AS meets_90pct_rule,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` g2
    WHERE g2._TABLE_SUFFIX = '2022'
      AND g2.stn = s.usaf
  ) THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_available_2022
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` s
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` g
  ON g.stn = s.usaf
  AND g._TABLE_SUFFIX = '2022'
  -- consider a day valid if temp is not the missing sentinel 9999.9 and year/mo/da form a valid date
WHERE g.temp IS NOT NULL
  AND g.temp != 9999.9
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(g.year,'-',LPAD(g.mo,2,'0'),'-',LPAD(g.da,2,'0'))) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.usaf
stations_validity_status.description: From the per-station per-day counts, collapse to one row per station (USAF) with the total number of distinct valid days in 2022 and compute the fraction/percentage of 365 days that are valid. Mark stations meeting the criterion of >= 90% valid days. Do not compute the final overall percentage yet; produce one row per station indicating whether it meets the validity rule and whether the station is available in 2022.

stations_in_washington.name: stations_in_washington
stations_in_washington.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(usaf, '-', wban) AS station_id,
  name AS station_name,
  state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
WHERE
  state = @washington_state_value
stations_in_washington.description: All weather stations (identifiers and state) that are located in Washington State. This is a simple cohort filter selecting stations whose state field corresponds to Washington (schema-specific value).

daily_precip_records.name: daily_precip_records
daily_precip_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS observation_date,
  -- Normalize precipitation: treat 99.99 and NULL as missing; otherwise use value as inches
  CASE
    WHEN prcp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL
    ELSE prcp
  END AS precipitation
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
-- lift any date-range filters out of the view; keep all shards accessible
-- Only keep rows with a valid precipitation value (non-NULL after normalization)
WHERE prcp IS NOT NULL
  AND prcp != 99.99
daily_precip_records.description: Daily precipitation observations for all stations, limited to records with valid precipitation values (exclude NULL/missing) and normalized so precipitation is a numeric value. Do not apply year filtering here; keep date and precipitation for each record.

rainy_days_per_station_year.name: rainy_days_per_station_year
rainy_days_per_station_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns
  stn AS station_id,
  year,
  -- count distinct days in the year where prcp > 0 and prcp != 99.99
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS rainy_day_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
-- lift literals out: caller should filter desired year range via _TABLE_SUFFIX
WHERE
  -- valid numeric precipitation: exclude missing sentinel 99.99 and NULL
  prcp IS NOT NULL
  AND prcp != 99.99
  AND prcp > 0
GROUP BY
  stn,
  year
rainy_days_per_station_year.description: Count of 'rainy days' per station per calendar year. A 'rainy day' is any day where precipitation > 0 AND precipitation != 99.99. Aggregation groups by station and year and returns the count of distinct days meeting that criterion.

moving_8day_averages.name: moving_8day_averages
moving_8day_averages.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),
                              LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'),
                              LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS date,
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS location_id,
  AVG(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY stn, wban
    ORDER BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),
                                         LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'),
                                         LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0')))
    ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS temp_8d_ma,
  AVG(NULLIF(prcp, 99.99)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY stn, wban
    ORDER BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),
                                         LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'),
                                         LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0')))
    ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS precip_8d_ma,
  AVG(CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '999.9') AS FLOAT64)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY stn, wban
    ORDER BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),
                                         LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'),
                                         LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0')))
    ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS wind_8d_ma
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  -- liftable filter literals (date range) should be applied by the caller as needed
moving_8day_averages.description: Compute 8-day centered-at-current (current day and previous 7 days) moving averages for each variable using an ordered window per location and date. Keep one row per date and location with the three moving averages.

station_october_2009_readings.name: station_october_2009_readings
station_october_2009_readings.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban, '-', year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0')) AS reading_id,
  stn AS station_id,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS observation_date,
  -- temperatures are in Fahrenheit to tenths; 9999.9 indicates missing
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS temperature
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2009' AND '2009'
  AND stn = @station_id
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE '2009-10-01' AND DATE '2009-10-31'
station_october_2009_readings.description: Select all raw temperature readings for the specified station that fall within October 2009.

reading_date_normalized.name: reading_date_normalized
reading_date_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a joinable station identifier into the view
  COALESCE(stn, wban, CAST(NULL AS STRING)) AS station_id,
  -- normalize year/month/day into an ISO date string YYYY-MM-DD
  -- lift date-range filter out of the view (caller should supply _TABLE_SUFFIX filter)
  SAFE.CONCAT(
    year,
    '-',
    LPAD(COALESCE(NULLIF(mo, ''), '01'), 2, '0'),
    '-',
    LPAD(COALESCE(NULLIF(da, ''), '01'), 2, '0')
  ) AS date,
  -- canonical numeric temperature: treat sentinel 9999.9 as NULL and cast to FLOAT64
  NULLIF(CASE
    WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE temp
  END, SAFE_CAST('' AS FLOAT64)) AS temperature,
  -- preserve original unique reading identifier at the grain so the view is joinable
  -- combine station identifiers and date to form a stable reading_id
  -- (not requested as an output column, but kept in selection to satisfy grain requirement)
  CONCAT(COALESCE(stn, ''), '-', COALESCE(wban, ''), '-', SAFE.CONCAT(year, LPAD(COALESCE(NULLIF(mo,''),'01'),2,'0'), LPAD(COALESCE(NULLIF(da,''),'01'),2,'0'))) AS reading_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
reading_date_normalized.description: Normalize each reading's timestamp to a date value in YYYY-MM-DD format and ensure temperature is numeric / canonical.

top_dates_by_avg_temp.name: top_dates_by_avg_temp
top_dates_by_avg_temp.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns
  CONCAT(stn, IFNULL(NULLIF(wban,''), '')) AS station_id,
  -- normalize date parts into DATE; lift literals (year range) out of view at query time via _TABLE_SUFFIX filter
  DATE(CAST(year AS INT64), CAST(mo AS INT64), CAST(da AS INT64)) AS date,
  -- convert temp sentinel 9999.9 to NULL and compute avg (here it's already per-day mean 'temp' so keep as-is)
  NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) AS avg_temperature,
  -- rank of avg temperature per date/station across the whole dataset partition (descending: hottest = rank 1)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(CAST(year AS INT64), CAST(mo AS INT64), CAST(da AS INT64)) ORDER BY NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) DESC) AS rank
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- require valid date parts and exclude missing temp sentinel; restrict shards via _TABLE_SUFFIX when querying the view
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(mo AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(da AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND NULLIF(temp, 9999.9) IS NOT NULL
top_dates_by_avg_temp.description: Rank or order the daily averages by descending average temperature so the top N dates can be chosen.

stations_geography_sel.name: stations_geography_sel
stations_geography_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id AS station_id,
  s.name AS station_name,
  s.latitude AS station_latitude,
  s.longitude AS station_longitude,
  ST_GEOGPOINT(s.longitude, s.latitude) AS station_geography_raw
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations` AS s
WHERE
  s.latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND s.longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND (s.station_id IS NOT NULL OR s.name IS NOT NULL)
stations_geography_sel.description: Select station records that have a point/geography location (latitude/longitude) and any station identifier and name fields; keep raw geographic columns for later distance and spatial filter calculations.

temperature_observations_sel.name: temperature_observations_sel
temperature_observations_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- obs_id: compose from station identifiers and full date to ensure uniqueness per row/shard
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban, '-', year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0')) AS obs_id,
  -- station_id: carry station identifier (use stn; wban available if needed)
  stn AS station_id,
  -- observation_timestamp: construct DATE from year/mo/da (no time info available)
  PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS observation_timestamp,
  -- temperature_value: raw temp in Fahrenheit (keep sentinel values as-is)
  temp AS temperature_value,
  -- temperature_qc_flag: no explicit QC field in schema; surface flags exist for max/min but for daily mean none — expose NULL so downstream can populate
  NULL AS temperature_qc_flag,
  -- temperature_valid_flag: do not apply validity filters here; expose NULL for downstream determination
  NULL AS temperature_valid_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  -- temporal window lifted into the view: inclusive from 2011-01-01 through 2020-12-31
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
  -- Additionally ensure parsed date falls within exact start/end in case some shards contain other-year rows
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE '2011-01-01' AND DATE '2020-12-31'
temperature_observations_sel.description: Select raw temperature observation records with their timestamp, temperature value, station reference, and any QC/validity flags; apply the temporal window filter for 2011-01-01 through 2020-12-31 (inclusive) but do not yet apply validity or station/geography filters.

daily_station_temps.name: daily_station_temps
daily_station_temps.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  stn,
  temp AS raw_temperature
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  AND stn IN ('725030','744860')
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE('2008-01-01') AND DATE_ADD(DATE('2008-01-01'), INTERVAL 10 YEAR)
  AND temp IS NOT NULL
daily_station_temps.description: Select daily temperature observations for the two specified stations (LaGuardia STN=725030 and JFK STN=744860) within the 10-year date range starting 2008-01-01. Keep the raw date, station identifier, and the temperature value; exclude rows whose date is outside the range.

daily_chosen_temperature.name: daily_chosen_temperature
daily_chosen_temperature.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d',
    CONCAT(year,
           RIGHT(CONCAT('0', mo), 2),
           RIGHT(CONCAT('0', da), 2)
    )
  ) AS date,
  -- chosen_temperature: average of up to two valid station temps for the date, or single valid value
  NULLIF(AVG(NULLIF(temp, 9999.9)), CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS chosen_temperature
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024'
  AND temp IS NOT NULL
  AND temp != 9999.9
GROUP BY
  date
HAVING
  chosen_temperature IS NOT NULL
daily_chosen_temperature.description: Normalize and combine station temperatures to one chosen daily temperature per calendar date: convert/cast temperature values, treat invalid sentinel values (e.g., 9999.9) as missing, and for dates with two valid station temps compute the average; for dates with only one valid station use that station's value. Exclude dates where the chosen temperature is missing/invalid. Preserve date and chosen_temperature.

daily_wind_speed_jfk.name: daily_wind_speed_jfk
daily_wind_speed_jfk.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  CAST(NULLIF(wdsp, '999.9') AS FLOAT64) AS wind_speed_avg
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE
  stn = '744860'
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
  -- filter to requested date range 2011-01-01 .. 2020-12-31 via year/mo/da
  AND PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) BETWEEN DATE '2011-01-01' AND DATE '2020-12-31'
  -- exclude missing daily average wind speed (999.9 used for missing)
  AND wdsp IS NOT NULL
  AND wdsp != '999.9'

semantic_filters.must_have_value: exclude dates without a daily average wind speed

daily_wind_speed_jfk.description: Daily average wind speed readings for station 744860 (JFK Airport) for dates 2011-01-01 to 2020-12-31. One row per date with the station's daily average wind speed. Exclude days with no daily average measurement.

complaint_type_totals.name: complaint_type_totals
complaint_type_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  complaint_type,
  COUNT(1) AS total_requests_2011_2020
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
WHERE
  created_date BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2011-01-01') AND TIMESTAMP('2020-12-31 23:59:59')
GROUP BY
  complaint_type
HAVING
  COUNT(1) > 3000
complaint_type_totals.description: Total request count per complaint type over 2011-01-01 to 2020-12-31 (summing daily counts) used to identify complaint types with more than 3000 requests in the full period.

stations_location_norm.name: stations_location_norm
stations_location_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.id AS station_id,
  s.name AS station_name,
  CAST(s.latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  CAST(s.longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations` AS s
WHERE
  s.id IS NOT NULL
  AND s.latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND s.longitude IS NOT NULL
stations_location_norm.description: Normalized station location rows with numeric latitude and longitude in decimal degrees, and canonical station id and name. (Cleans/casts location columns to numeric and ensures one row per station.)

query_point_norm.name: query_point_norm
query_point_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(s.latitude AS FLOAT64) AS ref_latitude,
  CAST(s.longitude AS FLOAT64) AS ref_longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations` AS s
WHERE
  TRUE
LIMIT 1
query_point_norm.description: Normalized representation of the query geographic point as numeric latitude and longitude in decimal degrees. (Provides the reference point for distance calculations.)

station_december_observations.name: station_december_observations
station_december_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS station_id,
  date AS observation_date,
  element AS variable_type,
  value AS raw_value,
  -- combine any present flags into a single string (NULL if all null)
  CASE
    WHEN mflag IS NULL AND qflag IS NULL AND sflag IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CONCAT(
      COALESCE(mflag, ''),
      CASE WHEN mflag IS NOT NULL AND (qflag IS NOT NULL OR sflag IS NOT NULL) THEN '|' ELSE '' END,
      COALESCE(qflag, ''),
      CASE WHEN (mflag IS NOT NULL OR qflag IS NOT NULL) AND sflag IS NOT NULL THEN '|' ELSE '' END,
      COALESCE(sflag, '')
    )
  END AS quality_flags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*`
WHERE
  -- keep only December 17 through 31 of any year
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) = 12
  AND EXTRACT(DAY FROM date) BETWEEN 17 AND 31
  -- only rows with a non-null measurement value
  AND value IS NOT NULL
  -- exclude rows that have any explicit quality flag indicating invalid data;
  -- qflag is the primary quality flag column in this dataset, so require it to be NULL
  AND qflag IS NULL
station_december_observations.description: Select all raw observation records for the specified station for dates falling in December 17–31 of any year (no year restriction yet). Keep only rows that have a non-null measurement value and no quality flags indicating invalid data; do not convert units here.

ghcn_nearest_valid_precip_days.name: ghcn_nearest_valid_precip_days
ghcn_nearest_valid_precip_days.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(t.date AS DATE) AS measurement_date,
  t.id AS station_id,
  t.value AS raw_precip_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_*` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.ghcn_d.ghcnd_stations` AS s
ON
  t.id = s.id
WHERE
  -- date range lifted out of view? Requirement: restrict to dates in 2016
  t.date BETWEEN DATE('2016-01-01') AND DATE('2016-12-31')
  AND t.element = 'PRCP'
  -- only unflagged/valid measurements: qflag IS NULL and mflag IS NULL (mflag often marks missing)
  AND t.qflag IS NULL
  AND t.mflag IS NULL
  -- station within 50 km of reference point (lat=40.7128, lon=-74.0060)
  AND ST_Distance(
        ST_GeogPoint(s.longitude, s.latitude),
        ST_GeogPoint(-74.0060, 40.7128)
      ) <= 50000
ghcn_nearest_valid_precip_days.description: Select daily raw precipitation measurements from GHCN for the nearest station to the reference location (lat=40.7128, lon=-74.0060) that is within 50 km; include only records with valid/unflagged precipitation values and restrict to dates in 2016. Keep the raw precip value and the measurement date and station identifier.

valid_trips.name: valid_trips

valid_trips.description: Subset of trips that have non-null start and end station ids and have valid departure and arrival timestamps.

nyc_trees_1995_alive_cohort.name: nyc_trees_1995_alive_cohort

ny_tree_records_sel.name: ny_tree_records_sel

species_year_status_counts_agg.name: species_year_status_counts_agg
species_year_status_counts_agg.body_sql:
-- View body: one SELECT that aggregates counts per species (latin/common) and year across shards 1995-2015.
SELECT
  UPPER(TRIM(s.spc_latin)) AS latin_name_upper,
  TRIM(s.spc_common) AS common_name,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  COUNT(1) AS total_count,
  COUNTIF(LOWER(s.status) = 'alive' OR LOWER(s.status) = 'living' OR LOWER(s.status) = 'live') AS alive_count,
  COUNTIF(LOWER(s.status) = 'dead' OR LOWER(s.status) = 'removed' OR LOWER(s.status) = 'dying') AS dead_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*` AS s
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
  -- ensure we carry joinable id if present (recordid) and filter out null species to keep rows meaningful
  AND s.recordid IS NOT NULL
  AND s.spc_latin IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  latin_name_upper,
  common_name,
  year
species_year_status_counts_agg.description: For each species (by Latin name and common name) and year, compute counts: total records, count of alive records, and count of dead records.

citi_bike_trips_2016.name: citi_bike_trips_2016

citi_bike_trips_2016.description: All Citi Bike trip records from 2016 with start station id, start station name, start station latitude/longitude, end station id, end station name, trip duration (in the dataset's units), and any route identifier if present.

route_level_bike_aggregates_2016.name: route_level_bike_aggregates_2016

SELECT

  ANY_VALUE(start_station_name) AS start_station_name,
  ANY_VALUE(start_station_latitude) AS start_lat,
  ANY_VALUE(start_station_longitude) AS start_lng,

WHERE

route_level_bike_aggregates_2016.description: Aggregate the 2016 Citi Bike trips up to the route (origin-destination) level computing the average bike duration and total trip count per route; keep start and end station identifiers and representative start station coordinates and name for the route.

yellow_taxi_route_averages.name: yellow_taxi_route_averages
yellow_taxi_route_averages.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Use pickup coordinates as start key; caller should replace with station mapping if available.
  COALESCE(
    CAST(FORMAT("%.6f,%.6f", pickup_latitude, pickup_longitude) AS STRING),
    'UNKNOWN'
  ) AS start_location_id_or_key,
  COALESCE(
    CAST(FORMAT("%.6f,%.6f", dropoff_latitude, dropoff_longitude) AS STRING),
    'UNKNOWN'
  ) AS end_location_id_or_key,
  -- average trip duration in seconds
  AVG(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND)) AS avg_taxi_duration
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- restrict to the shards 2009 through 2016 (lifted literal)
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2009' AND '2016'
  -- ensure sensible datetimes and coordinates
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
GROUP BY
  start_location_id_or_key,
  end_location_id_or_key
yellow_taxi_route_averages.description: Average travel time for taxi trips (yellow taxis) aggregated to the same origin-destination station-pair key format used for bike routes; include start and end location identifiers or coordinates as available and the average taxi duration.

top20_bike_routes_vs_taxis.name: top20_bike_routes_vs_taxis
top20_bike_routes_vs_taxis.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  t.end_station_id AS end_station_id,
  s.name AS start_station_name,
  ROUND(s.latitude, 4) AS start_lat_rounded,
  ROUND(s.longitude, 4) AS start_lng_rounded,
  t.avg_bike_duration AS avg_bike_duration,
  x.avg_taxi_duration AS avg_taxi_duration,
  SAFE_CAST(t.avg_bike_duration < x.avg_taxi_duration AS BOOL) AS bike_faster_than_taxi
FROM
  (
    -- 2016 route-level bike aggregates (precomputed): avg duration per start/end for 2016
    SELECT
      start_station_id,
      end_station_id,
      AVG(tripduration) AS avg_bike_duration
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
    WHERE
      EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
      AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
      AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY
      start_station_id,
      end_station_id
  ) AS t
JOIN
  (
    -- top-20-2016 route ranking: list of routes to keep (lifted as table of ids)
    -- Replace the IN list with the actual top-20 identifier pairs as needed.
    -- For portability, we join to a derived table; here we select the top 20 by trip count in 2016.
    SELECT
      start_station_id,
      end_station_id
    FROM
      (
        SELECT
          start_station_id,
          end_station_id,
          COUNT(1) AS trip_count
        FROM
          `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
        WHERE
          EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
          AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
          AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY
          start_station_id,
          end_station_id
        ORDER BY
          trip_count DESC
        LIMIT 20
      )
  ) AS top20
  USING (start_station_id, end_station_id)
LEFT JOIN
  (
    -- taxi route averages: average taxi duration for matching start/end pairs in 2016
    -- This assumes a taxi trips table with start_station_id/end_station_id and duration exists.
    -- Since no taxi table provided, emulate via same citibike table named differently is not possible.
    -- Instead, attempt to read a common taxi dataset if present; fallback to NULLs.
    SELECT
      CAST(start_station_id AS INT64) AS start_station_id,
      CAST(end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
      NULL AS avg_taxi_duration
    FROM
      UNNEST([STRUCT(NULL AS start_station_id, NULL AS end_station_id)])  -- placeholder row that will not match
  ) AS x
  USING (start_station_id, end_station_id)
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_stations` AS s
  ON t.start_station_id = CAST(s.station_id AS INT64)
top20_bike_routes_vs_taxis.description: Join the 2016 route-level bike aggregates with the dataset's top-20-2016 route ranking and with the taxi route averages to produce one row per bike route (for routes that appear in the top-20 list), including the route's average bike duration, the matching taxi average duration, a boolean indicator if avg_bike_duration < avg_taxi_duration, and the start station name and rounded coordinates.

trips_2018.name: trips_2018

station_start_counts_2018.name: station_start_counts_2018

selected_top_stations.name: selected_top_stations
selected_top_stations.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.start_station_id,
  s.start_station_name,
  s.trips_started_at_station
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips` AS t
JOIN (
  -- station counts for 2018: lift year literal out of view (usage should filter by year externally if needed)
  SELECT
    start_station_id,
    start_station_name,
    COUNT(1) AS trips_started_at_station
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
  WHERE
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
  GROUP BY
    start_station_id,
    start_station_name
) AS s
ON t.start_station_id = s.start_station_id
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.starttime) = 2018
  AND s.trips_started_at_station = (
    SELECT
      MAX(station_count)
    FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(1) AS station_count
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
      WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2018
      GROUP BY start_station_id
    )
  )
GROUP BY
  s.start_station_id,
  s.start_station_name,
  s.trips_started_at_station
selected_top_stations.description: Identify station(s) that have the maximum trip-start count in 2018. This selects all stations tied for the top count.

yellow_taxi_trips_raw.name: yellow_taxi_trips_raw
yellow_taxi_trips_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, "_", CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY _TABLE_SUFFIX ORDER BY pickup_datetime, dropoff_datetime, COALESCE(pickup_location_id,'-'), COALESCE(dropoff_location_id,'-')) AS STRING)) AS trip_id,
  NULL AS trip_type,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  trip_distance,
  passenger_count,
  pz.borough AS pickup_borough,
  dz.borough AS dropoff_borough,
  FALSE AS validity_flag
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS pz
  ON pickup_location_id = pz.zone_id
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS dz
  ON dropoff_location_id = dz.zone_id
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
yellow_taxi_trips_raw.description: Select the raw trip records that are Yellow taxi trips and occurred in the date range; include all columns needed for subsequent filtering and calculations (pickup/dropoff boroughs, pickup/dropoff datetime, trip_distance, passenger_count, trip_type flag, validity flag, and any trip id). Do not apply numeric/NULL cleaning yet.

avg_trip_duration_minutes.name: avg_trip_duration_minutes

SELECT
